authority.releaseOwner: Product Release Cut and Cut Transition protocols
authority.rule: The adapter verifies and transports owner bytes and roots. It does not derive identity from SemVer, channel labels, source paths, Shifu state, download archives, or caches.

material: installed product image bytes and safe relative symlinks

trustDomains.rule: Every bundled image retains its Release Cut publicationPolicy.trustDomain. Import verifies each domain independently and never upgrades shifu-local history into public history.

migration.source: Export requires a clean native cli_inventory_fsck result and a retained selected receipt; pending or ambiguous publication fails closed.
migration.preflight: Exit import verifies the complete member in a disposable clean config home before destination writes.
migration.copyForward: Import preserves source receipt roots as history, rebinds installed image productRoot fields to the destination, and writes a new generation-one copy-forward receipt before current.json.
migration.interruption: If current.json publication is interrupted after the receipt is durable, retry publishes only the selection bound by that exact receipt.
migration.idempotence: The same bundle and copy-forward receipt return already_present; a different generation-one receipt or current selection rejects.
migration.legacy: Qualified installed-image layouts are copied forward. Legacy bootstrap-only state without a selected installed image is not silently guessed and requires a separate explicit adapter.

compatibility.rollback: A portable rollback coordinate is re-rooted only when its exact predecessor image is present in the same bundle.
compatibility.labels: Product version and channel remain descriptive labels; Release Cut roots decide identity and movement.

included: typed activation, rollback, and update outcome receipts
excluded: full transcripts and unbounded terminal output
unrelated files outside the native product inventory

falsifiers: Import requires a deleted source archive, mutable channel cache, Shifu cache, or original product path.
A shifu-local Release Cut becomes public through export or import.
A destination productRoot is copied from the source instead of copy-forward rebound.
current.json is published before its generation receipt is durable.
An unknown required feature, entry kind, or receipt schema is ignored.
A rollback target absent from the bundle is guessed from SemVer or a mutable label.
nonClaims: No real user home is read, migrated, garbage-collected, or overwritten by qualification.
No public release is published and no platform support claim is broadened.
No physical-disk-loss, off-host backup, replication, or disaster-recovery guarantee is made.
